description: LOAD-4: measured latency of the dom-sales consumer sample under scripts/load/run_load.py at 100,000 order lines. A run is only comparable to another run of the same machine class, engine and row count; the numbers are a regression reference for this class of machine, not a promise to a customer.

environment.machine: developer laptop (Windows 11), load generator and application on the same machine
environment.engineMode: embedded file database, AUTO_SERVER, single JVM

findings.cause: the /by/<referenceField>/<id> finder compared LOWER(CAST(column AS TEXT)), which no index can serve, so every call scanned the whole table
findings.fix: a reference or uuid column holding a canonical UUID now compares natively; p95 587.8 ms to 21.9 ms at 8 users

findings.cause: the generated query controller ignored ?limit= on grouped queries, so 20,000 groups (1.5 MB) were returned for limit=50
findings.fix: the aggregate path reads the request limit like the plain path; the response is 4 KB, and the driver stops at the limit when there is no sort or HAVING

findings.cause: every per-concept query ran a second COUNT(*) with the same predicate even when the page was short
findings.fix: a short page answers the total (offset + size) without the count; p95 740.2 ms to 380.5 ms at 8 users

findings.cause: GROUP BY over every order line costs about 0.2 s per call in embedded H2 at 100,000 rows whatever the limit; a covering index (tenant_id, order_id, line_total) measured only about 30% faster, within run-to-run noise. Under 8 concurrent users the calls queue
findings.fix: none by SQL tuning; a total that must be read often belongs in a stored rollup, not a query over every row

findings.cause: throughput was 50.8 calls/s at 8 users and 50.2 calls/s at 40, so the machine is saturated near 50 calls/s and added users only queue; the 40-user latencies are queueing delay, not slow queries
findings.fix: none needed on this class of machine; a capacity figure for Postgres or multi-node needs a run on that setup

findings.cause: the embedded H2 file reached 12.5 GB for about 400,000 small rows after seeding and load runs. Established 2026-10-21 on H2 2.3.232 (REG-272): WRITE_DELAY=0 turns off the MVStore background thread, the only online compactor, and writes one chunk per commit, while the default RETENTION_TIME=45000 keeps every superseded chunk -- 20k rows + 20k event rows committed one at a time made a 662 MB file (~33 KB/row) that SHUTDOWN COMPACT reduced to 5.7 MB (~0.3 KB/row)
findings.fix: RETENTION_TIME=0 on the H2_LOCAL/H2_SERVER URLs (UserDatabaseDefinitionLoader + npdev_cli twin): the same run made 210 MB and 8 kill -9 cycles lost no acknowledged commit. Expected size with it: about 10 KB per committed row on a never-compacted dev file, about 0.3 KB per row after SHUTDOWN COMPACT. Apps generated before the fix keep the old URL until regenerated. Not done: online compaction (MVStore compactFile from the RuntimeHost, H2Local only, needs its own kill -9 durability proof) -- open a new item if dev disk use still hurts

thresholds.profile: 8 users; the 40-user run is a capacity record and is not expected to meet them
